\newcommand{\method}{RepRoute}

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}

Multimodal web agents must trade accuracy against inference cost: a task may
be as small as clicking one link or as long as a multi-step search session.
Representation routing manages the cost-accuracy trade-off with selective
classification over each request; the routing decision boundary is a simple
threshold, $y = x - 1$.

Prior work analyzes routing for web agents~\cite{wang2025routing}.
Benchmark studies of multi-step tool use report similar cost
profiles~\cite{chen2024agents} (see pp.~10--12 of the supplement).

Our method \method{} achieves 92\% accuracy. Representation routing reduces
inference cost by 4.23\% on average (11.58\% in the best case), with median
routing latency of 5 ms, as described in Section~\ref{sec:method}. Ablating
the router shifts accuracy by -0.8 points (p = .05).
